title: platform-policy-sources.v1
description: One file of the registered pages this Skill is allowed to read, and what each one is known to settle. The registry is every JSON file in references/sources/; all files share the same header fields. A rule question is answered from this list or it is not answered: an open-ended search reaches whichever page ranks well today, which is how a stale help page gets quoted as current.

platform.description: The platform that published the page. `other` is the cross-platform row - an archive or tracker covering several platforms - and is in scope only as a change_signal, never as a source. `bilibili` and `twitch` are first-class platforms like the rest, not cases `other` covers.

role.description: rule_source may be quoted in a verdict. change_signal may only send a run to a rule_source - it reports that something moved, never what the rule now says.

url.description: Null is allowed only on an unverified_draft, and means the page has not been located yet. That is a recorded hole, not permission to answer from somewhere else.

source_authority.description: Deliberately the same vocabulary as the monetization rule library, so a claim can move between the two without being relabelled.

verified_at.description: The date this page was last actually read. Non-null exactly when status is verified: a date here means somebody fetched it, never that somebody trusts it.

method.description: plain_fetch: the first HTTP body is the document. js_rendered: a plain fetch returns an empty client shell, but a JS render returns the article. The only retrieval path is the official_page_render_page tool, which renders such pages on official help hosts. browser_rendered: no retrieval path has returned a body yet, so a re-check without a browser reads silence as stability and the row cannot be verified.

watch_urls.description: Where a change to this page shows up - usually an announcement blog or newsroom. Not the same page, and that is the whole point.

watch_urls_absent_reason.description: Required whenever watch_urls is null. Forcing a sentence here is what stops 'nobody worked out where changes appear' from being silently indistinguishable from 'changes appear nowhere'.

does_not_carry.description: What this page is known NOT to state. Reading it saves the next run from concluding that a rule does not exist because the page it looked at was silent about it.

language.description: BCP-47 tag of the language the page is written in, such as en or zh. A quote stays in this language; a report delivered in a language with a different primary subtag owes each quote from this page a gloss.
